question: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oesophagus is most common in the lower third and is associated with Barrett's oesophagus and obesity, while adenocarcinoma is most common in the upper and middle thirds and is associated with alcohol and tobacco use.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false — the descriptions are reversed. Squamous cell carcinoma: upper/middle thirds, alcohol + tobacco. Adenocarcinoma: lower third, Barrett's oesophagus + GORD + obesity. These two subtypes have completely different demographics, risk factors, and anatomical locations.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement reverses the two subtypes. Squamous cell carcinoma occurs in the upper and middle thirds and is associated with alcohol, tobacco, and achalasia. Adenocarcinoma arises in the lower third from Barrett's metaplasia and is linked to chronic GORD and obesity. Never confuse these two profiles.
